info: In Russian, the imperfective aspect in the past tense describes an action as ongoing, repeated, habitual, or viewed without emphasis on its completion. It is often used for things that were happening, used to happen, or happened repeatedly. For example, Я читал means “I was reading” or “I used to read,” while Я читал каждый день means “I read every day” (as a repeated past activity). The imperfective does not necessarily mean the action was literally unfinished—it emphasizes the process, duration, or repetition rather than the result.

For example, Я читал means “I was reading” or “I used to read,” while Я читал каждый день means “I read every day” (as a repeated past activity). The imperfective does not necessarily mean the action was literally unfinished—it emphasizes the process, duration, or repetition rather than the result.
